ap_physics_c_mechanics-m02.stem: A light rod can rotate about a fixed pivot. A perpendicular force of $30\text{ N}$ pushes up on the rod at $0.4\text{ m}$ to the right of the pivot, and a perpendicular force of $25\text{ N}$ pushes up on the rod at $0.5\text{ m}$ to the left of the pivot. Take counterclockwise as positive, so the first force produces a positive torque about the pivot and the second a negative torque. What is the net torque about the pivot?

options.why: Uses the net force times the sum of the lever arms, $(F_1-F_2)(r_1+r_2)=4.50\text{ N·m}$.
Subtracts in the wrong order, $F_2r_2-F_1r_1=0.500\text{ N·m}$, which reverses the sense of the net torque.
Multiplies the forces by the same lever arm, $(F_1-F_2)r_1=2.00\text{ N·m}$.

ap_physics_c_mechanics-m03.stem: A boat coasts after its engine is shut off with velocity $v(t)=12e^{-t/2}$, where $v$ is in meters per second and $t$ is in seconds. What is the total distance that the boat travels as $t\to\infty$?

options.why: Integrates only up to $t=\tau$, $v_0\tau(1-e^{-1})=15.2\text{ m}$, instead of to infinity.
Divides the initial speed by the time constant instead of multiplying, $v_0/\tau=6.00$ in the wrong units.
Integrates $e^{-t/\tau}$ without the factor $\tau$ from the chain rule, giving $v_0=12.0\text{ m}$.
$\Delta x=\int_0^\infty v_0e^{-t/\tau}dt=v_0\tau=24.0\text{ m}$.

items.stem: How much net work does the force do on the block from $x=0$ to $x=7\text{ m}$?

options.why: Averages the force values at the plotted points and multiplies by the distance, $21.0\text{ J}$.
Uses only the first two segments, $32.0\text{ J}$, up to the point where the force is zero.

The signed areas are 24.0, 8.00 and -4.00 J, so the net work is $28.0\text{ J}$.

stimulus.description: Velocity of the block versus time

items.stem: What is the amplitude of the oscillation?

options.why: Divides the maximum speed by the period without the $2\pi$, $v_{max}/T=0.500\text{ m}$.
Multiplies the maximum speed by the period, $v_{max}T=2.00\text{ m}$.
Uses $v_{max}\cdot2\pi/T=3.14\text{ m}$, which is the maximum acceleration.
$v_{max}=A\omega$ with $\omega=2\pi/T$ gives $A=v_{max}T/(2\pi)=0.318\text{ m}$.

ap_physics_c_mechanics-f01.title: Experiment: rotational inertia of a disk from a falling mass

stimulus.description: A student wraps a light string around the rim of a horizontal disk of radius R = 0.1 m that rotates on a frictionless axle. A mass m hangs from the string and is released from rest. The student measures the acceleration a of the hanging mass for several values of m and wants to determine the rotational inertia I of the disk. Assume the string does not slip.

data.y_label: Acceleration of the hanging mass a (m/s^2)
notes: A student wraps a light string around the rim of a horizontal disk of radius R = 0.1 m that rotates on a frictionless axle. A mass m hangs from the string and is released from rest. The student measures the acceleration a of the hanging mass for several values of m and wants to determine the rotational inertia I of the disk. Assume the string does not slip.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe an experimental procedure to collect the data for the acceleration as a function of the hanging mass. Include the equipment and the measurements, how the independent variable is changed, and one way to reduce the uncertainty in the measured acceleration.
parts.model_answer: Measure each hanging mass with a balance; release it from rest and measure the distance it falls with a meterstick and the fall time with a stopwatch (or a photogate) to find $a=2h/t^2$; change only the hanging mass with the same disk, string and release height; reduce the uncertainty by repeating each release and averaging the times or by using a larger fall height.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies how the mass is measured and how the acceleration is found (fall distance and time, with $a=2h/t^2$)
required_elements: a way to measure the mass and a way to find the acceleration
common_errors: omits how the acceleration is found

rubric_rows.criterion: Changes only the hanging mass while using the same disk, string and release height (all three must be controlled)
required_elements: change only the mass and keep the disk, string and height

rubric_rows.criterion: Reduces the uncertainty by repeating each release and averaging, or by using a larger fall height or a photogate (any one earns the point)
required_elements: repeat and average or larger height or photogate (any one earns the point)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: For the system, $a=\dfrac{mg}{m+I/R^2}$. Identify the quantities that should be plotted on the vertical and horizontal axes so that the data produce a straight line whose slope can be used to find $I$.
parts.model_answer: $1/a=\dfrac1g+\dfrac{I}{gR^2}\cdot\dfrac1m$: plot $1/a$ on the vertical axis against $1/m$ on the horizontal axis; the slope is $I/(gR^2)$ and the intercept is $1/g$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies $1/a$ (vertical) versus $1/m$ (horizontal)

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: On a blank grid whose scale you choose, plot the data in a form that gives a straight line, and draw a best-fit line. Label the axes with quantities and units and use a scale that fills most of the grid.

rubric_rows.criterion: Axes are labeled with quantities and units and the scale fills most of the grid
common_errors: scale uses less than half the grid

rubric_rows.criterion: Plots the five points $(1/m, 1/a)$ accurately
Draws a straight best-fit line through the trend of the points

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Use the best-fit line to determine the rotational inertia $I$ of the disk. Show your work.
parts.model_answer: The slope is $I/(gR^2)\approx0.077$ in SI units, so $I=\text{slope}\cdot gR^2\approx0.0076\text{ kg·m}^2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the slope of the best-fit line using two points on the line (about 0.077; accept any value within 8 percent)
common_errors: uses data points rather than points on the line

rubric_rows.criterion: Relates the slope to the rotational inertia: slope $=I/(gR^2)$ so $I=\text{slope}\cdot gR^2$
Obtains $I$ of about 0.0076 with units of kg·m^2 (accept any value consistent with the student's own slope from D1)
alt_solutions: a value of I consistent with the student's own slope from D1
